requirement:
The coverage index MUST display the combined view selected under
{cite}`requirements.test-coverage.index.selection` and
{cite}`requirements.test-coverage.index.freshness`. It MUST show the number of
selected test attempts and summarize coverage excluded because it is stale,
unavailable, or from a historical build configuration. Detailed test identities,
run provenance, and per-test execution data MUST remain in the saved coverage
artifacts rather than being included in the generated book.

For first-party Rust files under
{cite}`requirements.references.rust_item_coverage`, the summary MUST compute
line coverage from the union of instrumented file-and-line locations in the
selected fresh records, including their associated child-process records.
Each location MUST count once in the denominator and count as covered when any
selected record has a positive execution count for it. Percentages MUST be
computed from those union counts rather than averaged across process reports.
A view with no instrumented lines MUST show coverage as unavailable. The index
MUST visibly identify incomplete coverage and MUST NOT imply that every current
test has coverage merely because all available records are valid.
rationale:
The four marked tests in `src/execution_coverage/book.rs` cover every obligation in `requirements.test-coverage.index.summary`.

**Combined view and attempt count.**
- `filtered_runs_union_latest_attempts_and_invalidate_with_saved_source` checks "2 selected test attempts" and "2/2 (100.0%)" when two tests are combined.
- It also checks "1 selected test attempts" after a record from another build configuration is added.

**Excluded coverage summarized.**
- `filtered_runs_union_latest_attempts_and_invalidate_with_saved_source` checks "stale coverage; recollect" and "historical build configuration".
- `maps_distinguish_no_runs_zero_hits_stale_and_incomplete_coverage` checks "1 stale test attempts", "1 unavailable test attempts" and "missing or unreadable coverage".
- Those unavailable cases cover failed, interrupted and diagnostic attempts, a missing profile, an uncaptured source and unreadable metadata.

**No detailed identities, provenance or per-test data in the book.**
- `gaps_omit_test_data_and_preserve_saved_profiles_and_sources` asserts that every generated chapter omits "Test runs and provenance", "binary / one", "habeas-coverage-test", "application/json", captured source text and the JSON payload.
- It also asserts that only "Coverage gaps" and "File notes:" chapters exist, and that the saved attempt and run files and the profile files remain unchanged on disk.
- `gaps_union_process_locations_and_omit_per_test_reports` makes similar omission assertions.

**Union of locations, counted once, with percentages from union counts.**
- `gaps_union_process_locations_and_omit_per_test_reports` uses a parent and a child process that both report `code.rs` line 1, plus `zero.rs`. It asserts "Line coverage: **2/4 (50.0%)**".
- That result needs line 1 counted once in the denominator, line 3 (count `u64::MAX`) covered, and line 1 covered because one process has a positive count.
- It also rules out averaging per-process percentages.
- `gaps_omit_test_data_and_preserve_saved_profiles_and_sources` computes the union directly, with `code.rs` line 2 at 0 in the parent and 7 in the child, and asserts three covered locations ("3/3 (100.0%)").
- `filtered_runs_union_latest_attempts_and_invalidate_with_saved_source` does the same across two separate test records.

**No instrumented lines.** `maps_distinguish_no_runs_zero_hits_stale_and_incomplete_coverage` records an attempt with no lines. It asserts "Coverage unavailable", no "Line coverage:" text, no "NaN" and "No usable instrumented lines". The no-runs case is also asserted.

**Incomplete coverage must be visible and not imply all current tests are covered.**
- `gaps_omit_test_data_and_preserve_saved_profiles_and_sources` asserts "not establish that all current tests were measured" even though every available record is valid.
- The incomplete and unavailable cases assert "missing or unreadable coverage" or "Coverage history is incomplete".

**First-party Rust scope.** The `vendor` and `.rs` filtering happens at collection time in `src/execution_coverage/runner.rs#fn[export]` and in `rust_files` in `src/rust_coverage.rs`. `src/execution_coverage/book.rs#fn[union]` and the summary code in `populate_in` do not filter. The summary tests use only plain first-party `.rs` fixtures. I treat that scope as a property of what is recorded, not a separate behavior of the summary, so I don't count it as a gap.

I found no unacknowledged gap and no {fixme} is needed.

text: :::{req} index.summary
The coverage index MUST display the combined view selected under
{cite}`requirements.test-coverage.index.selection` and
{cite}`requirements.test-coverage.index.freshness`. It MUST show the number of
selected test attempts and summarize coverage excluded because it is stale,
unavailable, or from a historical build configuration. Detailed test identities,
run provenance, and per-test execution data MUST remain in the saved coverage
artifacts rather than being included in the generated book.
For first-party Rust files under
{cite}`requirements.references.rust_item_coverage`, the summary MUST compute
line coverage from the union of instrumented file-and-line locations in the
selected fresh records, including their associated child-process records.
Each location MUST count once in the denominator and count as covered when any
selected record has a positive execution count for it. Percentages MUST be
computed from those union counts rather than averaged across process reports.
A view with no instrumented lines MUST show coverage as unavailable. The index
MUST visibly identify incomplete coverage and MUST NOT imply that every current
test has coverage merely because all available records are valid.
:::{req} index.selection
The coverage index MUST combine the most recent recorded test attempt for each
nextest binary and test name among the retained runs. "Most recent" MUST refer
to when the attempt started, including failed or interrupted attempts. A newer
filtered run MUST update only the tests it executes, leaving other compatible
test records available to the combined view. A newer attempt with missing or
unreadable coverage MUST be shown as unavailable rather than replaced with an
older successful attempt. Results from incompatible instrumented build
configurations MUST NOT be combined under
{cite}`requirements.test-coverage.storage.configuration`.
The main combined view MUST use the instrumented build configuration of the
most recently started recorded test attempt. Latest-per-test selection MUST
occur within that configuration. Records from other configurations MUST be
identified as excluded historical coverage. Configuration selection MUST use
recorded metadata without building or executing tests.
:::{req} index.freshness
Only records whose captured source inputs match the current project source and
whose build configurations are compatible MAY contribute execution counts to
the combined view of {cite}`requirements.test-coverage.index.selection`.
Records invalidated by a source change, or whose compatibility cannot be
established, MUST be identified as stale or unavailable and excluded from the
combined coverage totals. Their per-process reports and matching captured source
MUST remain retained in the build artifacts until those artifacts are removed.
:::{req} rust_item_coverage

During repository validation, Habeas MUST parse every first-party Rust source file: every `.rs` file among the sources reference discovery considers under {cite}`requirements.references.discovery`, except those under the project-root `vendor` directory. Each explicitly declared function or method, including trait methods and test helpers, and each struct, enum, and union is an item that can be covered. An item is covered when it has a valid `{impl}`, `{cite}`, or `{test}` reference to a defined requirement or named example, or a valid citation of the built-in `habeas:util` under {cite}`requirements.references.util`, in a Rust comment attached to it or within its body; or when its outline node, or an outline node containing it, is recorded with its current hash as an outline input of an evidence record, a citation review, or a site review. Outline inputs recorded from selected search snippets under {cite}`requirements.authoring.finish_search.inputs` MUST count alongside mandatory inputs and additional reads. Comments belong to items under {cite}`requirements.references.outline_comments`; a comment before a field, variant, or attribute inside an item belongs to that item. A named example MUST reference a requirement under {cite}`requirements.examples.definition`. A reference in a string literal, on an enclosing module or impl block, or only in an evidence input MUST NOT count for the items it encloses. Habeas MUST report a Rust parse failure instead of silently skipping the file. Only {cite}`requirements.references.coverage.tests` and {cite}`requirements.references.coverage.examples` make an uncovered item a validation error; other items without recent coverage are warned about under {cite}`requirements.references.coverage.report`.
